ops.title: ccx ship: pending native commit and child Git fixes cover the Xcode timeout
ops.body:
# ccx ship performance findings

The installed ccx v0.57.0 still calls `gt modify -c` when appending to a tracked Graphite branch. Existing local patches cover both that call and the Git executable inherited by Graphite. They belong to an active session and have not been released. No duplicate implementation was added.

## Confirmed cause and version

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/ccx --version` reports `v0.57.0`.
- `/Users/yasyf/Code/cc-context` is on main at `9e49501`, four commits beyond the v0.57.0 tag. It includes PR #18, the remote-trunk submit fix, but its `internal/cli/shipgt.go` still invokes `gtRun(... gtCommitArgv(...))` for commits. Earlier PRs #15 and #16 replaced stack inspection and submission, respectively; neither removed `gt modify`.
- Main's `internal/render/render.go:newCmd` passes the literal executable name to `exec.CommandContext`, and its `childEnv` does not change PATH. In the affected session `/usr/bin` precedes `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so Git resolves through Apple's `/usr/bin/git` into Xcode. Homebrew Git 2.55.0 is installed.
- The parent investigation measured the same ancestry query at 1.85 seconds with Xcode Git and below 0.01 seconds with Homebrew Git. The original ship timed out after ten minutes. The same ship with command-local `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH` created commit `c6f85983c9` and PR #18287 within seconds. These timings and the production ship result were supplied by the parent; this lane independently confirmed the source and installed version.

## Existing delivery state

- `/Users/yasyf/.claude/worktrees/cc-context/perf-git`, branch `yasyf/ship-perf-git`: uncommitted `internal/lookpath/git.go`, `git_test.go`, and `internal/render/render.go`. `lookpath.Bin` selects an executable Git outside the system stub directories. `render.newCmd` uses it for direct Git calls. `lookpath.GitPATH` and `render.childEnv` prepend its directory for child tools, including Graphite. `CCX_GIT` provides an explicit override.
- `/Users/yasyf/.claude/worktrees/cc-context/perf-commit`, branch `yasyf/ship-perf-commit`: uncommitted changes in `shipgt.go`, `ship.go`, `gtrestack.go`, and `stack.go`. Existing tracked branches append or amend through native `git commit`; `gtModifyRestack` uses the existing native replay implementation for affected descendants. `gt create` remains for new branches because that path creates Graphite metadata. Both ordinary and hunk-scoped commits use the new dispatch.
- `/Users/yasyf/.claude/worktrees/cc-context/perf-submit`, branch `yasyf/ship-perf-submit`: commit `985d576` overlaps Graphite requests and uses their responses for the report. Other performance lanes remain active.
- The live owner is Claude session `a95d76f5-45c1-4bc5-86f4-d74ac2fd3967`, PID 6677. Its full CLI tests were still running in the commit, metadata, fetch, and submit lanes during this investigation. GitHub reported no open cc-context performance PR at the final check.

## Validation

An isolated detached snapshot combined only the current Git-selection and native-commit patches. Original worktrees and installed binaries were not changed.

The local integration probe `TestCCXPerformanceGitChildren` ran with `/usr/bin:/bin` before `/opt/homebrew/bin`. It exercised a direct `render.RunCLI("git", ...)` and a `gt` shim that itself execs `git`. Both reported `git version 2.55.0`. The test passed in 0.50 seconds, package time 0.991 seconds:

```text
go test -count=1 -timeout 30s ./internal/render -run '^TestCCXPerformanceGitChildren$' -v
git: git version 2.55.0
gt: git version 2.55.0
PASS
```

The probe source is `/tmp/ccx-performance-git-children-probe.go`; it uses a Homebrew-zsh shebang to keep the fixture outside the system executable delay. Snapshot patches are `/tmp/ccx-perf-git-snapshot.patch` and `/tmp/ccx-perf-commit-snapshot.patch`. The Git snapshot patch contains the tracked render integration; the two new lookpath files are separately preserved beside it.

The original Git-resolution package tests did not pass cleanly on this machine: `TestBinPrefersAGitOutsideTheStubDirs` and `TestGitPATHLeadsWithTheResolvedGitsDirectory` each exhausted the 15-second fake-Git version-probe timeout. Their fake executable uses `/bin/sh`. This proves a validation problem in the current candidate, so the pending change must not be described as fully verified. The isolated broader render run and real-fixture `TestShipGTNoPush` were stopped after remaining active for minutes; no green native-commit test verdict is claimed. Only this lane's test processes were stopped. The owner's tests remain untouched.

## Separate PR association follow-up

The parent observed that successful native API submission opened PR #18287, but `gt merge --dry-run --no-interactive` initially said the branch had no associated PR. A narrow `gt submit --no-edit --no-interactive --no-stack` reported no changes and refreshed the local association; the next merge dry run recognized the PR.

Neither the current perf-submit commit nor perf-meta's diff persists that association. The native submit path writes `gtmeta.RecordSubmitted`, whose SQL updates only `last_submitted_version`; returning the API's PR information for reporting does not update Graphite's branch-to-PR metadata. Record this with the active performance work for a focused follow-up: a newly API-created PR should be recognized by a subsequent `gt merge --dry-run` without another submit. No changes were made to the owner's active submit or metadata files.

The remaining delivery steps are the existing owner's validation, integration, PR, and release or coordinated installation. The existing `plugin/bin/ccx` modifications in the main checkout and performance worktrees were preserved. No global PATH or installed binary was changed.
